1→Perfect for reviewing any portion of the Torah reading.
     2→
     3→Choose a Parsha - including double Parshiot - and start practising right away. Makes practising easier - anytime, anywhere!
     4→
     5→The traditional Tikkun Korim places the 'Chumash' text on the right and the 'Torah' text on the left. This project was made with mobile one-handed usage on small-screened devices in mind. We came up with a simple way to get the most out of the small screen, by simply tapping to remove the Trop and Nikkud.
     6→
     7→**תיקון קוראים לחמשה חומשי תורה**
     8→
     9→**INSTRUCTIONS:**
    10→
    11→* Select a Chumash then a Parsha then an Aliya.
    12→* Tap the text to switch from with Nikkud and Trop/Taamim/Simanim to without. And vice versa.
    13→* Tap the back button on the top of the screen to go to the previous menu.
    14→* Tap the grid (four squares) to start from the beginning.
    15→* Quickly switch from one Aliya to the next by tapping the arrows on the top left.
    16→

## COMPREHENSIVE PROJECT ANALYSIS: Tikkun Korim

### PROJECT OVERVIEW

**Tikkun Korim** (תִּקּוּן קוֹרִאים) is a React-based web application for practicing Torah reading (Tikkun Korim). It displays Hebrew text from the Five Books of Moses with support for:
- Nikud (vowel points) and Trop (cantillation marks) toggle
- Navigation between Seforim (books), Parshas (sections), and Aliyot (subsections)
- Traditional Tikkun Korim two-column layout
- Mobile-friendly single-handed usage
- Keyboard navigation (vim-style and arrow keys)

---

### TECHNOLOGY STACK

**Core:**
- React 19.1.1 with TypeScript 5.5.4
- Vite 5.4.8 (build tool with React SWC plugin)
- React DOM 19.1.1

**Key Features:**
- RTL (Right-to-Left) Hebrew text support
- Custom Hebrew font: "ShlomosemiStam" from Shlomo-semiStam-lehaderes.ttf
- Responsive design with CSS Grid and Flexbox
- Modern CSS (glass-morphism, animations, gradients)
- Type-safe with strict TypeScript

---

### PROJECT STRUCTURE

```
src/
├── App.tsx                          # Main application component
├── index.tsx                        # React entry point
├── App.css                          # Global styles
├── index.css                        # Base styles + font loading
├── components/
│   ├── Header/                      # Top navigation & controls
│   ├── ParshaNavigation/            # Parsha selection menu (262 LOC)
│   ├── InfiniteAmudScroll/          # Main text display (163 LOC)
│   ├── TextLine/                    # Individual text line rendering
│   ├── AmudDisplay/                 # Amud (page) container
│   ├── Footer/                      # Bottom footer
│   ├── Toast/                       # Toast notifications (NEW)
│   ├── LoadingSpinner/              # Loading indicator
│   └── index.ts                     # Component exports
├── hooks/
│   ├── useTikkun.ts                 # Main state management (166 LOC)
│   ├── useKeyboardNavigation.ts      # Keyboard input handling (73 LOC)
│   └── useScrollNavigation.ts        # Scroll-related logic
├── utils/
│   ├── navigationUtils.ts           # Parsha/Aliya finding logic (272 LOC)
│   ├── hebrewUtils.ts               # Hebrew text processing (131 LOC)
│   ├── dataLoader.ts                # Data loading utility (113 LOC)
│   ├── index.ts                     # Utility exports (NEW)
│   └── testNavigation.ts            # Testing helpers (52 LOC)
├── data/
│   ├── parshadata.ts                # Parsha/Aliya metadata (5,921 LOC)
│   ├── tikkunData.ts                # Full Torah text data (158,059 LOC)
│   └── constants.ts                 # Hebrew numeral mappings
├── types/
│   └── index.ts                     # TypeScript interfaces
└── assets/
    └── fonts/                       # Hebrew font files
```

**Total Codebase:** ~165,762 lines (mostly data files)

---

### KEY FEATURES & COMPONENTS

#### 1. **State Management (useTikkun Hook)**
- Manages: current amud, page visibility, nikud toggle, word gap, loading state
- Features:
  - Lazy-loads Torah data on mount
  - Detects current parsha from amud position
  - Provides navigation functions
  - Exposes navigation API to window for testing (`window.tikkunNav`)
  - NEW: `targetLine` state for precise line-level navigation

#### 2. **Navigation System**
- **navigateAmud()**: Move between pages (next/prev or direct number)
- **navigateToParsha()**: Jump to specific sefer/parsha/aliya
- **navigateParshaDirection()**: Move to next/previous parsha
- **getCurrentParshaFromAmud()**: Detect which parsha is currently displayed
- **findAmudForParshaAliya()**: Locate amud number for given parsha/aliya combo

#### 3. **Keyboard Navigation**
Maps:
- ArrowLeft/h: Previous amud
- ArrowRight/l: Next amud
- ArrowUp/k: Previous parsha
- ArrowDown/j: Next parsha
- N/Space: Toggle nikud

#### 4. **Hebrew Text Processing**
- Removes/preserves vowel points (nikud)
- Handles Kri/Ksiv (reading variants vs. written text)
- Processes special layouts (satum/patuch)
- Manages word spacing for readability when nikud is hidden

#### 5. **Parsha Navigation Menu** (NEW)
- Interactive modal with search
- Three-level selection: Seforim → Parshas → Aliyot
- Shows current selection path
- Quick action buttons (home, reset)
- Responsive grid layout

#### 6. **Toast Notifications** (NEW)
- Success/info/warning/error message display
- Auto-dismiss after configurable duration
- Clean animation and styling

#### 7. **Infinite Amud Scroll**
- Renders all 248 amudim for full Torah coverage
- Intersection Observer to detect visible content
- Scroll-to behavior with smooth navigation
- Special handling for amud 78 (different layout)
- Prevents scroll conflicts during programmatic navigation

---

### DATA STRUCTURE

**Amud Object:**
```typescript
{
  amud: number;
  lines: Array<{
    number: number;
    fragments: string[];           // HTML text with Kri/Ksiv markers
    meta: Array<{                  // Perek/Pasuk metadata
      sefer: number;
      perek: number;
      pasuk: number;
    }>;
    aliyot: number[];              // Aliyah numbers for this line
    layout: 'satum' | 'patuch';    // Text layout style
  }>;
}
```

**Parsha Data (parshadata.ts):**
- 5 Seforim (Books): בראשית, שמות, ויקרא, במדבר, דברים
- 54 Parshas total
- 7-8 Aliyot per parsha (defined as perek:pasuk ranges)
- Example: בראשית Parsha 1 Aliya 1 = "1:1 2:3"

---

### CURRENT STATE & ISSUES

#### On Branch: `new-design`

**Staged Changes (Ready to commit):**
1. App.tsx - Component structure updates
2. Header/Header.tsx & Header.css - UI enhancements
3. Header/ParshaNavigation.tsx - New navigation menu
4. Toast/Toast.tsx & Toast.css - NEW notification system
5. useKeyboardNavigation.ts - Keyboard handler updates
6. useTikkun.ts - State management additions
7. New files: navigationUtils.ts, index.ts (utils), testNavigation.ts

**Unstaged Changes (In progress):**
1. **App.tsx**: Added targetLine prop to InfiniteAmudScroll
2. **useTikkun.ts**: 
   - Added `targetLine?: number` to TikkunState
   - Initialize targetLine to undefined
   - Clear targetLine on regular amud navigation
   - Pass targetLine to InfiniteAmudScroll when navigating to parsha
   - Log both amud AND line when navigating: `'Navigating to amud:', location.amud, 'line:', location.line`
3. **InfiniteAmudScroll.tsx**: NEW 85+ lines of scroll-to-line functionality
   - scrollToAmudAndLine() function for targeting specific lines within amudim
   - Uses IntersectionObserver with higher precision
   - Prevents intersection observer conflicts during programmatic scrolling
   - Proper cleanup of timeouts

**Design Changes (aesthetic):**
- Modern styling with glassmorphism effects
- Hebrew-friendly RTL layout
- Gradient backgrounds with animated overlays
- Responsive design for mobile

---

### POTENTIAL ISSUES & OBSERVATIONS

1. **Large Data Files**: tikkunData.ts is 158,059 lines - performance concern for initial load
   - Currently lazy-loaded via dynamic import (good!)
   - Consider: splitting into chunks or streaming if adding more features

2. **targetLine Integration**: Unstaged changes are incomplete
   - InfiniteAmudScroll has new scroll-to-line logic but changes not staged
   - navigateToParsha() now passes targetLine but this is in progress
   - Suggests feature is in active development

3. **Hebrew Font Loading**: 
   - Relies on custom font file (Shlomo-semiStam-lehaderes.ttf)
   - Uses @font-face with swap display - good for performance
   - Should verify font file exists in assets/fonts/

4. **Word Gap Algorithm**: 
   - Uses simple wordSpacing CSS (wordGap * 2px)
   - Only applied when nikud is OFF
   - Range: 1-6 (legacy constraint)

5. **Intersection Observer Complexity**:
   - Two competing observers: one for programmatic scroll, one for tracking visible content
   - Uses scrollingRef flag and timeout to prevent conflicts (robust approach)
   - Could be simplified with better separation

6. **Untracked Files**:
   - `.claude/` and `.entire/` directories (likely IDE/tool-specific)

7. **Type Safety**:
   - Types are well-defined (Amud, Line, Meta, ParshaLocation)
   - Some 'any' casts in navigationUtils.ts for aliya data lookups (minor issue)

8. **Testing & Navigation Debugging**:
   - testNavigation.ts exists with helper function
   - Navigation API exposed to window for console testing (useful!)
   - No formal test suite detected

---

### WORKFLOW SUMMARY

**User Flow:**
1. App loads → useTikkun loads tikkunData
2. Initial parsha detected from amud 1
3. User: keyboard keys OR clicks ParshaNavigation menu
4. navigateToParsha() finds amud and line
5. InfiniteAmudScroll scrolls to position
6. IntersectionObserver updates header with current location
7. TextLine renders Hebrew with/without nikud
8. Toast shows feedback

**Developer Features:**
- Open console and type: `tikkunNav.testNavigation()`
- Direct navigation: `tikkunNav.navigateToParsha("בראשית", "בראשית", 1)`

---

### FILES SUMMARY

| File | LOC | Purpose |
|------|-----|---------|
| tikkunData.ts | 158,059 | Full Torah text with metadata |
| parshadata.ts | 5,921 | Parsha/Aliya reference data |
| navigationUtils.ts | 272 | Parsha/amud finding logic |
| ParshaNavigation.tsx | 262 | Navigation UI menu |
| InfiniteAmudScroll.tsx | 163 | Main text display |
| useTikkun.ts | 166 | Core state management |
| hebrewUtils.ts | 131 | Hebrew text processing |
| dataLoader.ts | 113 | Data loading utility |
| Header.tsx | 109 | Top navigation bar |
| App.tsx | 122 | Root component |
| useKeyboardNavigation.ts | 73 | Keyboard handlers |

---

### CONCLUSION

This is a well-structured, feature-rich Torah reading practice application with:
✓ Strong TypeScript typing
✓ Clean component architecture
✓ Efficient lazy-loading of massive datasets
✓ Robust navigation system
✓ Mobile-friendly (RTL, Hebrew fonts, responsive)
✓ Modern UI with good UX feedback (toasts, animations)
✓ Active development (new-design branch with staged commits)

**Current Focus:** Adding line-level precision scrolling for better UX when navigating to specific aliyot within an amud.
